title: Dynamic bilinear network models
text: dynamic bilinear model estimates past network interactions predict future interactions, predictive mapping changes time. core equation : Θt=AtΘt−1Bt⊤+M+εt\Theta_t = A_t \, \Theta_{t-1} \, B_t^\top + M + \varepsilon_t Θt\Theta_t latent interaction state time tt (n×nn \times n matrix), AtA_t BtB_t time-varying sender receiver influence matrices, MM baseline mean capturing persistent dyad-specific tendencies. parameter tells : AtA_t (sender influence): n×nn \times n matrix entry ai,′,ta_{,',t} measures strongly actor ′'’s past behavior sender predicts actor ii’s current sending behavior. Large positive values indicate ii follows echoes ′'; negative values indicate opposing patterns. BtB_t (receiver influence): Entry bj,j′,tb_{j,j',t} captures past targeting actor j′j' predicts current targeting jj. reveals shifting alliances targeting patterns. MM (baseline mean): Captures stable, time-invariant dyad-specific tendencies. large MijM_{ij} indicates persistent tendency actor ii interact actor jj, regardless dynamics. σ2\sigma^2 (process variance): much unexplained variation remains latent network accounting bilinear dynamics. τA2\tau_A^2, τB2\tau_B^2 (innovation variances): rapidly influence matrices change one period next. Large values mean influence structure reorganizing quickly; small values mean relatively stable. τA2\tau_A^2 near zero, data favor static influence structure. ρA\rho_A, ρB\rho_B (AR(1) coefficients, optional): persistent influence matrices . Values near 1 indicate strong persistence; values near 0 indicate rapid mean reversion. See methodology page working paper full mathematical treatment.

text: Implements Dynamic Bilinear Network (DBN) models analyzing temporal relational data. Supports ordinal (rank likelihood), continuous (Gaussian), binary (probit) outcome types across static, dynamic, low-rank, HMM model variants unipartite bipartite directed networks. Includes functions model estimation via MCMC, visualization, impulse response analysis, diagnostics.

title: dbn: Dynamic Bilinear Network Models for Ordinal Relational Data — dbn-package
text: Bipartite HMM/lowrank HMM low-rank models currently support unipartite (square) networks. Bipartite data produce informative error. Use model = "dynamic" bipartite networks. Dynamic binary small networks dynamic model family = "binary" may encounter numerical singularities network fewer ~15 nodes. warning issued model entry. Consider model = "static" larger network. HMM label switching Regime numbering (1, 2, ..., R) HMM model arbitrary may differ across MCMC chains. Compare regimes estimated /B matrices, label. Lowrank Stiefel identifiability orthonormal factor matrix U low-rank model identified orthogonal rotation. Factor loadings \(\alpha_t\) U interpreted together.

title: dbn 0.2.0
text: Four model types: static, dynamic, low-rank, HMM (regime-switching). Three outcome families: ordinal (rank likelihood), Gaussian, binary (probit). Full bipartite network support static dynamic models (n_row != n_col). OpenMP-parallelized /B row/column updates thread-safe RNG. Impulse response analysis (compute_irf(), build_shock()). Posterior predictive distribution generation PPC plots. Memory-aware dynamic model: auto time-thinning, optional Z storage, estimate_memory(). Warm start support via previous argument continuing MCMC chains.
